fields.text: Distilled and bottled by Rusty Anchor Spirits, Key West, FL

prompt:
You are assisting a US TTB (Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau) compliance
agent who is reviewing an alcohol beverage label. Optical character recognition
has already run on this image and failed to read the fields listed below — the
photograph is blurred, badly lit, at an angle, or has glare.

Your job is to READ, not to judge. You are not deciding whether this label
complies with anything, and you are not being asked whether the label matches an
application. Another system does that. Report only what is physically printed on
the image.

Fields still needed:
- brand: the brand name in display type — the label's own name for the product. Not the producer's corporate name in the small print at the bottom, unless the same words also appear as the display brand
- class_type: the class or type designation, e.g. "Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey", "London Dry Gin", "Bordeaux Superieur"
- abv: the alcohol content exactly as printed, e.g. "45% Alc./Vol. (90 Proof)"
- net_contents: the net contents exactly as printed, e.g. "750 mL"
- producer: the bottler or producer name from the "Bottled by" / "Produced by" / "Distilled by" statement

Rules:
- Transcribe exactly as printed, preserving capitalization, punctuation and
  spacing. "STONE'S THROW" is not "Stone's Throw".
- If a field does not appear on this image, return null for it. Do not infer it
  from the beverage type, the producer, or anything else on the label. A missing
  field reported as null is a useful answer; a guess is a harmful one.
- If you can make out only part of a field, return the part you can actually
  read and lower your confidence accordingly.
- confidence is 0 to 1 and should reflect legibility, not plausibility.
